keypoints.name: Resistance
keypoints.description: Resistance is introduced as a property that opposes current flow in both AC and DC circuits, causing a decrease in current magnitude. It's explained using a water analogy with a narrow nozzle.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Resistance is introduced early, explained with an analogy, and revisited when summarizing the three primary factors.  It is described in multiple contexts throughout the video.
representative_quotes: resistance opposes the flow of current

keypoints.name: Reactance (Inductive & Capacitive)
keypoints.description: Reactance is presented as the property causing current to either lag (inductive) or lead (capacitive) the voltage in AC circuits. Inductive and capacitive reactance are explained using water wheel and elastic chamber analogies respectively.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Reactance is a major focus, explained in detail using water analogies to represent inductors and capacitors, and compared to resistance. The differences between inductive and capacitive reactance are emphasized.
representative_quotes: inductive reactants causes the current to lag behind the voltage
capacitive reactants causes the current to lead the voltage

keypoints.name: Impedance
keypoints.description: Impedance is presented as the cumulative effect of resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance. It signifies how a component modifies the current within a circuit.
keypoints.strength_reasoning: Impedance is introduced in the late part of the video, defined as the sum of all factors, and then reinforced during the ending summary. Although a dedicated concept, it's brief.
representative_quotes: impedance of a component signifies how it modifies the current within a circuit
the cumulative effect of these factors is referred to as impedance
